classification.classification_note: The reproduced memory error is a 1-byte out-of-bounds stack write: `readstat_copy_quoted()` fills the 1024-byte destination and then appends a NUL terminator at index 1024.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 1033-byte witness is SPSS command text beginning `SEt C="` and containing exactly 1024 bytes between the quotes. In `readstat_parse_spss_commands`, the Ragel `double_quoted_string` rule records that payload as `str_start` plus `str_len = 1024`, and `quoted_string` routes it into `copy_quoted_buf`, which calls `readstat_copy_quoted(buf, sizeof(buf), str_start, str_len)` with stack `char buf[1024]`. Inside `readstat_copy_quoted`, the truncation guard clamps `this_len >= buf_len` down to `buf_len` instead of `buf_len - 1`, so a 1024-byte quoted string is treated as fully copyable even though the helper still appends a terminator. The saved witness contains no backslashes, so the escape-aware loop copies one byte into `buf` for each of the 1024 iterations and leaves `j == 1024`. The final `buf[j] = '\0'` therefore writes one byte past the end of the 1024-byte stack buffer. Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `readstat_copy_quoted`, and ASan identifies `buf` in `readstat_parse_spss_commands` as the overflowed stack object.

source.code: double_quoted_string = "\"" ( [^"]* ) >{ str_start = fpc; } %{ str_len = fpc - str_start; } "\"";
source.description: First project-code parser action that materializes the attacker-controlled quoted value into the start pointer and length used by the vulnerable copy helper.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 1033 bytes long and has the form `SEt C="<1024-byte payload>" `, with exactly 1024 bytes between the quotes and no backslashes. When the closing quote is reached, this rule sets `str_start` to the first byte after the opening quote and `str_len` to 1024.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The helper appends a terminator one byte past the 1024-byte stack destination.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `readstat_copy.c:45:12` and identifies `buf` in `readstat_parse_spss_commands` as the overflown stack object occupying `[224, 1248)`. The invalid write is at offset 1248, which is exactly index 1024 of `char buf[1024]`.

root_cause.description: The truncation logic keeps `this_len` equal to the full destination size instead of reserving one byte for the trailing NUL.
root_cause.note: When the caller passes a 1024-byte quoted string into a 1024-byte destination, this branch leaves `this_len == buf_len == 1024`. The loop can therefore consume the entire destination, and the later terminator write has no in-bounds slot left. The missing obligation is the same one already implemented in `readstat_copy()`: cap at `buf_len - 1` before writing `\0`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness directly feeds the entire staged witness into `readstat_parse_spss_commands`, so the input enters the SPSS command parser without any outer format or container dispatch.

tainted_value_origin.code: double_quoted_string = "\"" ( [^"]* ) >{ str_start = fpc; } %{ str_len = fpc - str_start; } "\"";
tainted_value_origin.description: This rule captures the exact attacker-controlled quoted substring and computes the `str_len` value that later becomes `this_len` in `readstat_copy_quoted`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the staged witness, the quoted payload begins immediately after the `SEt C="` prefix and ends at the closing quote 1024 bytes later, so this rule produces `str_len = 1024`.

fine_trace.code: double_quoted_string = "\"" ( [^"]* ) >{ str_start = fpc; } %{ str_len = fpc - str_start; } "\"";
fine_trace.note: Source. The witness prefix `SEt C="` enters the double-quoted-string rule, and when the closing quote is reached this action records the quoted payload boundaries. For the exact staged witness, the captured payload length is 1024 bytes, so `str_len` becomes 1024.

This grammar rule routes the captured quoted token into the `copy_quoted_buf` action. On the witnessed `SET` command, that control choice means the 1024-byte value is copied into stack `buf`, not into the smaller `string_value` buffer used by value-label parsing.

The `copy_quoted_buf` action passes the captured substring into `readstat_copy_quoted` with `sizeof(buf) == 1024`. ASan later identifies this `buf` stack object as `[224, 1248)` in `readstat_parse_spss_commands`.

Root cause. With `str_len == 1024` and `buf_len == 1024`, this clamp keeps `this_len` at 1024 instead of reserving one byte for the trailing NUL. The helper therefore commits to processing a full-buffer-length string.

The exact staged witness has 1024 bytes inside the quotes and no `\\` bytes, so the escape-suppression path never consumes a character without incrementing `j`. The loop therefore copies one byte into `buf` on each of the 1024 iterations, fills `buf[0..1023]`, and exits with `j == 1024`.
Sink. After step 5 leaves `j == 1024`, this terminator write targets `buf[1024]`, one byte past the last valid element of `char buf[1024]`, matching the saved ASan `WRITE of size 1`.

poc.trigger: The staged 1033-byte `poc` is SPSS command text of the form `SEt C="<1024-byte payload>" `, with exactly 1024 bytes between the quotes and no backslashes. Parsing that quoted value through `copy_quoted_buf` makes `readstat_copy_quoted()` fill the 1024-byte stack `buf` and then write the terminator at `buf[1024]`, reproducing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow write.

format.name: SPSS command text
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged shape `SEt C="<1024-byte payload>" `: case-insensitive `SET`, identifier `C`, opening quote, 1024 payload bytes that contain neither `"` nor `\\`, closing quote, trailing space. When Ragel closes that quote, `str_len` becomes 1024 and `copy_quoted_buf` calls `readstat_copy_quoted(buf, 1024, ...)`; because the vulnerable clamp leaves `this_len == 1024`, the helper fills `buf[0..1023]` and the final `buf[j] = '\0'` lands at `buf[1024]`. A trailing `.` is unnecessary for this witness because the overflow happens immediately after the quoted token is copied, before full-command parse completion.
